title: Semi-Regularity Solving-Degree Overestimation
summary: The semi-regularity estimate may substantially exceed the actual solving degree in overdefined systems; characterize the conditions and parameter regimes where this occurs.

formal_statement.body: For polynomial systems arising in overdefined constructions, characterize the conditions and parameter regimes under which the solving-degree estimate $D_{\mathrm{sol}}$ obtained from the semi-regularity assumption is substantially larger than the system's actual solving degree. The unresolved comparison is motivated by the presence of many newly defined syzygy relations, which can invalidate the assumption underlying the estimate, and determining the actual solving degree is difficult in practice because it requires computing a Gr?bner basis.

scope.domain: Solving-degree analysis for polynomial systems from overdefined cryptographic constructions, including the effect of syzygies.
assumptions: Semi-regularity is assumed when deriving the solving-degree estimate.
parameters: D_sol: the semi-regularity-based estimate compared with the system's actual solving degree
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the conditions and parameter regimes in which D_sol is substantially larger than the actual solving degree.

citations.label: Modelling Ciphers with Overdefined Systems of Quadratic Equations: Application to Friday, Vision, RAIN and Biscuit

progress.summary: The paper explicitly poses this as a natural question motivated by new syzygies that can undermine semi-regularity-based estimates. It notes that checking the actual solving degree is difficult because doing so requires computing a Gröbner basis.
